title: Molecular basis for the regulation of retroviral nucleosomal integration by chromatin compaction.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 15675341 listing via its application programming interface: exactly 4 files, all .pdb atomic-coordinate models (7.2-7.4 MB each), licence CC-BY-4.0, 45 downloads. I downloaded HIV_Trinucleosome_Single_site.pdb and parsed it: 90,905 atoms, 2 chains (A, B), zero MODEL records, so it is one single static complex, not an ensemble and not a scored pose list. I also unzipped the publisher supplement: 25 files, of which 24 are figure images and one 13.3 MB Word document; parsing that document's XML showed 0 tables and only 5 embedded images, i.e. supplementary figure legends plus figures and no numeric data.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the gel-based in vitro integration and nucleosome-bridging assays were quantified from three independent experiments with standard deviations and t-tests (read in the figure legends and methods); those numbers appear only inside figure images, never as a table. Also from the text only: the HADDOCK 2.4 web-server protocol, the 2.0 angstrom clustering cutoff, the named active residues used to restrain docking, and the source structures 6L4A, 9C9M, 3S3M and 1KX5.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo deposit is open, CC-BY-4.0, no login; I downloaded one 7.4 MB coordinate file successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FIRST KILLER. There is no label column anywhere. The entire deposit is 4 protein-DNA coordinate files; the supplementary Word file contains 0 tables (verified by parsing it). Any prediction target (integration efficiency, interface accessibility, docking score) would have to be constructed from scratch, mostly by reading values off bar charts in figure images.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs as such are present: full atomic coordinates and therefore sequences for intasome and nucleosome chains in the 4 PDB files. But with no label, having inputs is moot.

a4_units_stated.note: No data table exists, so no units column exists. Assay units (percent integration, arbitrary autoradiography units) appear only in figure axes inside images.

a5_enough_rows.note: Four structural models, verified in the Zenodo file listing. The wet-lab side is roughly a dozen assay conditions at n = 3 replicates, read from figure legends. Orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row floor.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~29 MB (4 PDB files) plus a 14 MB supplement zip
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; I held one file in memory and counted its 90,905 atoms in under a second.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The data statement says only 'structural models have been deposited'; 4 models is consistent with the figures. No count disagreement because almost no counts are claimed.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only machine-readable quantity derivable here is the HADDOCK score / interface geometry of poses that HADDOCK itself produced. That is another program's output, so training on it would distil HADDOCK rather than learn biology - the circularity failure the checklist warns about.

existing_models.name: DeepHINT (deep neural network for HIV-1 integration site prediction, Bioinformatics 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to predict HIV-1 integration sites from surrounding genomic sequence and context; I found the paper listing in search results but did not retrieve the paper, so I am not quoting a number or a split.

backbone.name: none applicable
backbone.licence: Data is CC-BY-4.0, but there is nothing to fit a head on.

integration.join_key: PDB identifiers (6L4A, 9C9M, 3S3M, 1KX5) are present, but 4 structures cannot anchor a join that produces a training set.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this deposit; the published genome-wide integration-site datasets that would support such a question belong to other papers, not this one.

controls.positive_control: None definable - no model, no held-out quantity.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is available from this deposit: with four static docking models and no numeric assay table, any model trained here would only be describing four hand-built structures.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use nucleosome surface structure to predict how easily a virus's integration machine can reach its target site.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need many nucleosome (DNA wrapped on histone proteins) surfaces with a measured accessibility or integration efficiency for each; this paper supplies 4 structures and about a dozen gel assay conditions at 3 replicates each.
plain_idea.predict: Integration efficiency or interface accessibility. The true answer would come from radiolabelled in vitro integration assays read off polyacrylamide gels, which this paper reports only as bar charts inside figure images.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: HIV researchers and gene-therapy vector designers care which chromatin states a virus can integrate into, but this paper's data cannot train anything; at most it provides 4 structures as illustrative inputs.

ml_idea: No viable machine-learning project. The only idea the deposit supports - learning to reproduce HADDOCK docking poses or scores for intasome-nucleosome complexes - fails twice: 4 examples is far too few, and the target would be another program's output. The paper's real quantitative content (integration efficiency across chromatin compaction states) was never released as numbers.

effort.compute_note: Measured directly: the 4 deposited files total about 29 MB and one parsed in under a second with a few hundred MB of memory. No cross-validation estimate is meaningful because there is no training set.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Zenodo file listing - it names 4 .pdb files and nothing else. That single application-programming-interface call, which takes seconds, kills the project.

verdict_reason: The deposited data is 4 protein-DNA docking models and nothing else (verified by downloading and parsing one, and by confirming the 13 MB supplementary Word file contains 0 tables). Part A fails on A2 (no label column exists; it would have to be digitised from gel bar charts in figure images), A5 (4 structures; wet-lab side is about a dozen conditions at n = 3) and A8 (the only machine-readable quantity would be HADDOCK's own docking score, so a model would distil HADDOCK, not biology). A4 also fails for want of any data table. This is a fine mechanistic structural-biology paper and a non-starter as a machine-learning dataset.
